sections.history: Thirumanimadam, also called Manimadakkoil, stands in the village of Thirunangur near Sirkazhi, in the Chola Nadu of the old Tamil country. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and one of the eleven Thirunangur Tirupathis, all sung by Thirumangai Alvar in his Periya Thirumozhi. The presiding Lord is Narayana Perumal, with the Goddess Pundarikavalli; the shrine is also known as the Badrinarayana Perumal temple. No inscription or royal patron is firmly recorded, so its age rests on the Alvar's hymns, placed between the seventh and ninth centuries. Of the eleven shrines, this is the one where all of them meet.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian temple whose sanctum stands on a raised platform, reached by a flight of steps. Above it rises the Pranava vimana, named for the sacred syllable Om. Lord Narayana is worshipped here with the Goddess Pundarikavalli. Because the eleven utsavars of the group are brought to this temple for the Garuda Sevai, its precinct serves as the common ground of the Thirunangur shrines.
sections.legends: Tradition holds that after the death of the Goddess, Shiva's grief became a fierce dance that multiplied him into eleven Rudras at Thirunangur. The Rudras asked Narayana to show himself to them, and the Lord appeared in eleven forms; each was installed in a separate temple, and these are the Thirunangur Divya Desams. At Manimadam he is Narayana, and it is here that the eleven come together each year.
sections.festivals: The great day is the Garuda Sevai, on or around the day after Thai Amavasai (January–February), when the utsavars of the eleven shrines arrive at Thirumanimadam on Garuda vahanas and Thirumangai Alvar's mangalasasanam is celebrated in the Mangalasasana Utsavam. Tradition holds that seeing all eleven together equals visiting each one.
sections.experience: If you can, plan around the Garuda Sevai, when all eleven shrines meet in one place. On ordinary days this is a quiet village temple, a good first stop before walking or driving on to the other Tirupathis through the paddy fields, about 10 km by road from Sirkazhi.

visit.timings: Darshan is generally held in morning and evening sessions with a midday break; the Garuda Sevai day is by far the busiest. Confirm timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thirunangur lies about 10 km by road south-east of Sirkazhi (Sirkali) in Mayiladuthurai district. Sirkazhi, on the Chennai–Mayiladuthurai railway line, is the nearest station, and Tiruchirappalli, about 160 km away, the nearest major airport. Auto-rickshaws and taxis from Sirkazhi reach the village; the eleven shrines lie among paddy fields close to one another.
